## How `z.string().transform(fn)` is represented

`.transform()` is not its own core node — it is sugar that wraps the string in a **pipe**. The classic `ZodType` method list defines the signature `transform<NewOut>(...): ZodPipe<this, ZodTransform<Awaited<NewOut>, core.output<this>>>` (`packages/zod/src/v4/classic/schemas.ts:131-133`), and implements it as `return pipe(this, transform(tx))` (`:245-247`). Two classic factories build the nodes:

- `transform(fn)` returns `new ZodTransform({ type: "transform", transform: fn })` (`classic/schemas.ts:2291-2298`; the class/interface is at `:2243-2249`).
- `pipe(in_, out)` returns `new ZodPipe({ type: "pipe", in: in_, out: out })` (`classic/schemas.ts:2555-2566`; class at `:2538-2553`).

So a transformed string is a `$ZodPipe` whose `in` is the `$ZodString` and whose `out` is a `$ZodTransform`; the user function lives in `def.transform` (`core/schemas.ts:3824-3827`). The parallel core-level builder is `_transform` (`core/api.ts:1477-1487`). The string itself is built by `string()` → `core._string(ZodString, params)` (`classic/schemas.ts:617-621`).

## Order of input parsing and transformation

The pipe runs its input first, then its output: core `$ZodPipe._zod.parse` (`core/schemas.ts:4432-4446`) runs `def.in._zod.run(payload, ctx)` (the string parse), then hands the result to `handlePipeResult(left, def.out, ctx)`. `handlePipeResult` (`core/schemas.ts:4449-4456`) forwards `left.value` into `def.out._zod.run(...)`, and only *that* node is the transform. The transform node's parse calls `def.transform(payload.value, payload)` (`core/schemas.ts:3844-3864`). The classic `ZodTransform` re-installs its own `_zod.parse` (wrapping `addIssue`, `classic/schemas.ts:2257-2287`), so the classic body executes, but the effect is the same: the string is validated, then the transform receives the validated value. The transform is not re-validated as input — it sets `optin = "optional"` (`core/schemas.ts:3841`) and throws `$ZodEncodeError` in backward direction (`:3845-3847`). `$ZodType.run` wires parse-then-checks, with the synchronous forward path at `core/schemas.ts:314-321`.

## Which input issues stop the pipe; the issue-code exception

`handlePipeResult` (`core/schemas.ts:4449-4456`): if `left.issues.some((iss) => iss.code !== "unrecognized_keys")`, it sets `left.aborted = true` and returns the payload **without running the transform** — "Any issue stops the pipe, so a failing refinement never feeds its transform" (`:4450`). The single exception is **`unrecognized_keys`**: such an issue describes the input's extra properties, not the piped value, and may be reconciled by an enclosing intersection, so it does *not* stop the pipe. (By contrast the codec path, `handleCodecAResult` `:4510-4515`, aborts when `result.issues.length` is non-zero with no such carve-out.)

## How the transformed value is carried onward

`payload.value = _out; return payload` — the transform overwrites the payload's value in place (`core/schemas.ts:3862-3863`; async branch `:3850-3855`; a Promise under a sync ctx throws `$ZodAsyncError` at `:3858-3859`). `handlePipeResult` then feeds `left.value` into `def.out` (`:4456`). At the top, core `_parse` (`core/parse.ts:22-37`) builds `ctx = { async: false }`, calls `schema._zod.run({ value, issues: [] }, ctx)`, throws `$ZodAsyncError` if a Promise (`:26-28`), throws the error if `result.issues.length` (`:29-33`), and otherwise returns `result.value` (`:34`). `_safeParse` returns `{ success: true, data: result.value }` (`core/parse.ts:71-79`). The classic surface binds these: `parse = core._parse(ZodRealError)`, `safeParse = core._safeParse(ZodRealError)` (`classic/parse.ts:8-33`).

## How `z.string().transform(fn)` is represented

`.transform()` is not its own core node — it is sugar that wraps the string in a **pipe**. The classic `ZodType` method list defines the signature `transform<NewOut>(...): ZodPipe<this, ZodTransform<Awaited<NewOut>, core.output<this>>>` (`packages/zod/src/v4/classic/schemas.ts:131-133`), and implements it as `return pipe(this, transform(tx))` (`:245-247`). Two classic factories build the nodes:

- `transform(fn)` returns `new ZodTransform({ type: "transform", transform: fn })` (`classic/schemas.ts:2291-2298`; the class/interface is at `:2243-2249`).
- `pipe(in_, out)` returns `new ZodPipe({ type: "pipe", in: in_, out: out })` (`classic/schemas.ts:2555-2566`; class at `:2538-2553`).

So a transformed string is a `$ZodPipe` whose `in` is the `$ZodString` and whose `out` is a `$ZodTransform`; the user function lives in `def.transform` (`core/schemas.ts:3824-3827`). The parallel core-level builder is `_transform` (`core/api.ts:1477-1487`). The string itself is built by `string()` → `core._string(ZodString, params)` (`classic/schemas.ts:617-621`).

## Order of input parsing and transformation

The pipe runs its input first, then its output: core `$ZodPipe._zod.parse` (`core/schemas.ts:4432-4446`) runs `def.in._zod.run(payload, ctx)` (the string parse), then hands the result to `handlePipeResult(left, def.out, ctx)`. `handlePipeResult` (`core/schemas.ts:4449-4456`) forwards `left.value` into `def.out._zod.run(...)`, and only *that* node is the transform. The transform node's parse calls `def.transform(payload.value, payload)` (`core/schemas.ts:3844-3864`). The classic `ZodTransform` re-installs its own `_zod.parse` (wrapping `addIssue`, `classic/schemas.ts:2257-2287`), so the classic body executes, but the effect is the same: the string is validated, then the transform receives the validated value. The transform is not re-validated as input — it sets `optin = "optional"` (`core/schemas.ts:3841`) and throws `$ZodEncodeError` in backward direction (`:3845-3847`). `$ZodType.run` wires parse-then-checks, with the synchronous forward path at `core/schemas.ts:314-321`.

## Which input issues stop the pipe; the issue-code exception

`handlePipeResult` (`core/schemas.ts:4449-4456`): if `left.issues.some((iss) => iss.code !== "unrecognized_keys")`, it sets `left.aborted = true` and returns the payload **without running the transform** — "Any issue stops the pipe, so a failing refinement never feeds its transform" (`:4450`). The single exception is **`unrecognized_keys`**: such an issue describes the input's extra properties, not the piped value, and may be reconciled by an enclosing intersection, so it does *not* stop the pipe. (By contrast the codec path, `handleCodecAResult` `:4510-4515`, aborts when `result.issues.length` is non-zero with no such carve-out.)

## How the transformed value is carried onward

`payload.value = _out; return payload` — the transform overwrites the payload's value in place (`core/schemas.ts:3862-3863`; async branch `:3850-3855`; a Promise under a sync ctx throws `$ZodAsyncError` at `:3858-3859`). `handlePipeResult` then feeds `left.value` into `def.out` (`:4456`). At the top, core `_parse` (`core/parse.ts:22-37`) builds `ctx = { async: false }`, calls `schema._zod.run({ value, issues: [] }, ctx)`, throws `$ZodAsyncError` if a Promise (`:26-28`), throws the error if `result.issues.length` (`:29-33`), and otherwise returns `result.value` (`:34`). `_safeParse` returns `{ success: true, data: result.value }` (`core/parse.ts:71-79`). The classic surface binds these: `parse = core._parse(ZodRealError)`, `safeParse = core._safeParse(ZodRealError)` (`classic/parse.ts:8-33`).
